The cascade entry retroactively sources a claim the codebase and llms.txt had been making in their own words since launch. Every entry was fetched on its lastVerified date; none is remembered.

claims.claim: Reading pixels back from a canvas tainted by cross-origin data throws
claims.value: drawing cross-origin data without CORS approval taints the canvas; toBlob(), toDataURL() and captureStream() then throw a SecurityError
claims.sourceTitle: MDN — Allowing cross-origin use of images and canvas
claims.note: Fetched from MDN on 2026-07-31; the wording on the page is a paraphrase of the 'Security and tainted canvases' section, not a quote. This is browser security behaviour rather than a dated announcement, so it decays far more slowly than the package rows above — but it is the load-bearing technical claim on /dom-to-png, so it is recorded rather than assumed.

claims.claim: The naming and lifecycle rules a custom element must satisfy
claims.value: the name must start with a lowercase letter and contain a hyphen; observedAttributes is a static array of attribute names, and attributeChangedCallback() fires after an observed attribute is initialised when the declaration is first parsed
claims.note: Fetched from MDN on 2026-08-01. The hyphen rule is quoted on the page; the first-parse timing of attributeChangedCallback() is paraphrased. Both are load-bearing for the argument that a share-image widget belongs in a custom element, so they are recorded rather than assumed. Spec behaviour decays slowly, but MDN revises wording and this entry is what catches it.

claims.claim: Which declaration wins between a shadow tree and the outer document
claims.value: in cascade sorting order, when declarations come from different encapsulation contexts the outer context wins for normal rules and the inner context wins for important rules
claims.sourceTitle: W3C — CSS Cascade and Inheritance Level 5
claims.note: Fetched from the W3C TR on 2026-08-01. This is the normative source for a claim the codebase and llms.txt had been making in their own words since launch — that ::slotted() rules 'lose to your own CSS'. MDN's ::slotted and Using-shadow-DOM pages were both checked first and neither states the cascade direction, so the spec is the citation. The claim is now sourced everywhere it appears rather than asserted.
